# 🛒 The Supermarket Shelf Shuffle: Why the Aisles Keep Moving

A supermarket is not just a place where products wait for shoppers. It is also a carefully planned map.

That map often changes. A trade publication says stores update layouts to make the shop feel fresh, guide customer movement, highlight seasonal offers, and encourage impulse buying.

But a new layout can also support healthier shopping.

Researchers tested this in a group of UK supermarkets. Some stores changed their layout, while similar stores did not, so the two groups could be compared.

The changes were practical. The fruit and vegetable area became larger and moved closer to the entrance. Frozen vegetables were moved to a more visible aisle. Sweets were removed from displays near the checkouts and replaced with non-food items and water.

The effect was clear for fruit and vegetables. Sales rose sharply — by roughly 6,000 extra portions per store each week at first, growing to nearly 10,000 a few months later.

Snack sales moved the other way at first, dropping by more than a thousand portions a week. But that drop did not hold up as a clear, lasting trend.

Total sales for the whole store showed no clear change. The new layout did not seem to make people buy more overall — it changed what they bought.

A related survey found a similar pattern at home: shoppers using the changed stores reported buying more fruit and vegetables, with little clear effect on snacks.

### The shelf can shape the shopping mood

Another study looked at how shoppers feel while they shop. It found links between store layout, atmosphere, shoppers' feelings, and impulse buying. This does not prove that one shelf move causes a purchase. It shows that the shopping environment can be part of the decision-making process.

### Rearrangement can be driven by data

Some shelf changes are more than a visual refresh. Researchers have proposed using purchase data itself to decide which products should share an aisle, aiming to maximize impulse buying. In tests, this approach performed more consistently than simple manual changes — though it was not tested directly in real stores.

## In one line…

Supermarket shelves keep moving because space is never neutral: it can make healthier products easier to notice, or make impulse buying easier to trigger.

verified_claims_summary: Vogel et al.（2021）の研究は、英国の値引き型スーパー6店舗（介入3・対照3）を対象とする前向きマッチド対照クラスター研究で、介入は6か月実施された。店舗は無作為化されていないが、検証対象の記事は無作為化研究だとは断定していない。([journals.plos.org](https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pmed.1003729))
介入内容として、生鮮果物・野菜売り場の拡大と入口付近への移動、冷凍野菜の入口側通路への移動、レジおよびレジ向かいの通路端からの菓子類撤去、非食品・水などへの置換が確認できる。([journals.plos.org](https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pmed.1003729))

果物・野菜の売上増は3か月時点で1.71標準偏差、約6,170ポーション、6か月時点で2.42標準偏差、約9,820ポーション相当であり、記事の数値要約と一致する。菓子類売上も3か月時点で約1,359ポーション減少したが、6か月時点の差は統計的に明確ではなかった。([journals.plos.org](https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pmed.1003729))
店舗全体の総売上には統計的に有意な差がなく、女性参加者では果物・野菜の購買傾向と3か月時点の食事の質が改善した一方、菓子類購買への明確な介入効果は確認されなかった。記事の要約と整合する。([journals.plos.org](https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pmed.1003729))

Mantratzis et al.（2023）のギリシャのフィールド研究は205人を対象とし、店舗レイアウト・雰囲気などの小売環境要因が感情反応と衝動買い行動に関連するという要約を示している。記事は因果関係を断定しておらず、適切に慎重な表現になっている。([ruomoplus.lib.uom.gr](https://ruomoplus.lib.uom.gr/bitstream/8000/1824/1/paper_matranzis.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Edirisinghe and Munsonの研究は、購買データとassociation rule miningを用いて店舗全体の商品配置を定期的に再編し、衝動買いを最大化する方法を提案したもの。視覚的な棚替えや複数の既存手法を一貫して上回ったという結果と、実店舗での直接検証が今後の課題であるという説明は、記事と一致する。([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0957417422024617?utm_source=openai))

The Global Display Solutionの記事は、動線、季節商品、目新しさ、レジ周辺の衝動買い促進などを小売レイアウトの実務上の理由として説明しており、記事の導入部の要約を概ね裏付ける。ただし、これは査読付き研究ではなく業界向け解説である。([theglobaldisplaysolution.com](https://www.theglobaldisplaysolution.com/blog/6-modern-grocery-store-design-ideas-that-optimize-display-layouts/))
sources: Vogel et al., “Altering product placement to create a healthier layout in supermarkets,” PLOS Medicine（一次論文）。([journals.plos.org](https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pmed.1003729))

Mantratzis et al., “Exploring the Impact of Supermarket Store Layout and Atmospheric Elements on Consumer Behavior,” Journal of Operations and Strategic Planning。([ruomoplus.lib.uom.gr](https://ruomoplus.lib.uom.gr/bitstream/8000/1824/1/paper_matranzis.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Edirisinghe and Munson, “Strategic rearrangement of retail shelf space allocations: Using data insights to encourage impulse buying,” Expert Systems with Applications。([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0957417422024617?utm_source=openai))

The Global Display Solution, “6 Modern Grocery Store Design Ideas That Optimize Display Layouts,” 2025年5月6日。([theglobaldisplaysolution.com](https://www.theglobaldisplaysolution.com/blog/6-modern-grocery-store-design-ideas-that-optimize-display-layouts/))
fact_result.notes: 記事の中心的な具体的主張は確認でき、明確な矛盾はない。厳密には「snack sales」はVogel論文の測定対象である「confectionery sales（菓子類売上）」より広い表現だが、結論を変えるほどの誤りではない。また、Vogel研究は店舗無作為化ではないが、記事は無作為化と明記していない。
